haiku-low.q1: It does not differ. Both take the same failure path with equal timing (bcrypt runs on a dummy hash) and return the same 401 page, "Invalid email or password".
haiku-low.q2: It gets a 429 at once. The server does not check the password or read users, and the locked attempt is not counted.
haiku-low.q3: The server deletes the existing session row for the incoming cookie in the same transaction. A new session with a fresh random ID is issued; the old ID is never reused.
haiku-low.q4: Only an opaque random session ID, with no user data. The cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
haiku-low.q5: At 12 hours after login, the absolute cap (absolute_expires_at). Each request restarts the 30-minute idle clock, but it can never pass that cap.
haiku-low.q6: It deletes the matching session row if one exists, clears the cookie, and redirects with 302 to /login. Missing, unknown and expired IDs get the same result.
haiku-low.q7: The server runs DELETE FROM sessions for the cookie's hash before replying with a cleared cookie and 302 /login. If the row is already gone, it still counts as success with the same response.
haiku-low.q8: In Postgres, in the sessions table. Any instance hashes the cookie ID and looks up that row, so either instance can serve the request.
haiku-low.q9: In the login_attempts table in Postgres, keyed by lowercased email. The server counts rows with attempted_at within the last 10 minutes of the database's now().
haiku-low.q10: It compares the cookie's hash with a sessions row whose expires_at is still in the future. When valid, one atomic UPDATE sets expires_at to the earlier of now+30 minutes and absolute_expires_at.
haiku-low.q11: A 503 page, "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Please try again in a moment." with Retry-After: 5 and Cache-Control: no-store. No session is issued.
haiku-low.q12: A job on each instance every 5 minutes deletes expired sessions, old login attempts and passed lockouts, with one instance sweeping per run. A request that finds an expired row also deletes it.

sonnet.q1: It doesn't differ. Both take the same failure path and get the same 401 login page "Invalid email or password". An unknown email still runs bcrypt on a dummy hash, so timing matches.
sonnet.q2: The 5th failure sets a 15-minute lockout, so the next attempt gets a 429 login page right away. No users read and no bcrypt run. The locked attempt isn't counted.
sonnet.q3: On success the old session row (found by the hash of the incoming cookie) is deleted. A new session with a fresh random ID is inserted and the incoming ID is never reused.
sonnet.q4: Only an opaque random ID (32 CSPRNG bytes, base64url) and no user data. The cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts can't read it.
sonnet.q5: At the 12-hour absolute cap (login + 12 hours). Activity renews the 30-minute idle expiry but never past that cap.
sonnet.q6: The UPDATE returns zero rows. The server deletes the session row if one exists, clears the cookie and sends 302 /login.
sonnet.q7: If a cookie is present it runs DELETE FROM sessions WHERE id_hash before replying. If no such row exists that still counts as success. It then clears the cookie and sends 302 /login. With no cookie it skips the delete and sends the same response.
sonnet.q8: In Postgres, in the sessions table. Either instance hashes the cookie's ID with SHA-256 and looks up that id_hash in the shared database.
sonnet.q9: In the Postgres login_attempts table (failed attempts only, keyed by lowercased email), with lockouts in login_lockouts. The window is a sliding one: it counts rows where attempted_at > now() - 10 minutes, using the database clock.
sonnet.q10: It checks that expires_at > now() (database time) for the session's id_hash. If so, one atomic UPDATE sets expires_at = LEAST(now + 30 min, absolute_expires_at) and returns user_id.
sonnet.q11: A 503 page: "Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Please try again in a moment." It carries Retry-After: 5 and Cache-Control: no-store. No session is issued and no cookie is set.
sonnet.q12: A job on each instance every 5 minutes deletes sessions with expires_at < now(). pg_try_advisory_lock lets only one instance sweep per run. A request that finds an expired row also deletes it.
